video_caption: The video segment opens with a white and black humanoid robot (Atlas from Boston Dynamics) crouching on a blue block in what appears to be a warehouse or lab, with yellow caution tape visible in the background. The robot then performs a backflip, landing perfectly on the block, as three then four "shocked face" emojis appear around it. The robot stands and raises its arms in triumph. Suddenly, Elon Musk, wearing a dark suit, appears in the bottom left, looking thoughtfully at the robot, while the emojis remain visible. The scene transitions to a dark background with digital code falling, and then to a web browser showing a Twitter (now X) post by Elon Musk. Musk, still in his suit, is positioned to the left of the browser as a large blue Twitter bird logo appears on the right. The highlighted tweet reads: "This is nothing. In a few years, that bot will move so fast you'll need a strobe light to see it. Sweet dreams..." and is dated November 26, 2017. A voiceover reads the tweet, and a reply from Christian Davis asking "How would a strobe light help see anything?" is shown, followed by Musk's reply: "Otherwise you'd only see a blur." The video then transitions to an abstract shot of a futuristic engine, followed by two tilted images appearing against a digital code background: one of a sleek, futuristic car, and the other of Marty McFly from "Back to the Future Part II" holding a pink hoverboard.

The video segment opens with a humanoid robot, resembling a Tesla Bot/Optimus, with a black head, white torso, and metallic grey limbs, picking up a blue toy block from a yellow tray and placing it into a blue tray, with the overlaid text "It can be trained to conduct new tasks, such as un-sorting." (English). The robot then performs a stretching pose in an indoor setting, accompanied by the text "And after a long day of work, time to stretch!" (English). The scene transitions to multiple robots, including two humanoid robots similar to Boston Dynamics Atlas and two quadrupedal robots resembling Boston Dynamics Spot, performing synchronized dance moves in a large, open indoor facility with a blue padded floor and large windows. Next, a computer screen displays a "Isaac Gym" simulation interface showing numerous grey humanoid robots walking, running, and even performing a cartwheel on a checkered grey and white floor, highlighting various body parts and simulation parameters on the left-hand panel. This is followed by an outdoor scene where four people, dressed in casual theme park-like vests and shirts, walk alongside three small, grey and white quadrupedal robots with blue accents in a themed environment reminiscent of a sci-fi village or a Disney park. The video then transitions to a dark background with glowing blue and white digital lines and particles, featuring a red hexagonal logo with an abstract grey robot head/gear and the text "Hardware.ai" below it, before displaying "FEATURE SERIES" (English) in the center. The segment concludes with a man, with short brown hair and tattoos on his arms, wearing a white t-shirt that reads "ALL YOU NEED IS Y = 1/X Y²+X² = 9 L" (English), speaking and gesturing against the same digital background, referencing a previous video where he used reinforcement learning to teach a robotic dog to move forward.

A man with short, light brown hair and a beard, wearing a white t-shirt with the graphic "ALL YOU NEED IS 1/x = y, x^2 + y^2 = 9, y = |-2|x|" (mathematical equations and the word "LOVE" formed by a graph), gestures with his hands while speaking against a dark background featuring falling white alphanumeric characters. The scene then transitions to a computer-generated animation of multiple orange, quadrupedal robots on a grey and white checkered floor, with one robot in the foreground crawling and shuffling its legs close to the ground, followed by a wider shot showing several such robots. The video cuts back to the man, who continues to gesture as the text overlay "*for a movement task" appears, followed by a black screen displaying white text of Python-like code titled "# velocity tracking reward". This code defines `lin_vel_error` and `ang_vel_error` calculations. Below the code, text explains "lin_vel_error = the difference between command given to move (forward/backward/left/right) and actual linear velocity of the robot" and "ang_vel_error = same for angular commands (turning left or right)", with an additional note "the rewards are scaled in accordance with multipliers set in config file". This is followed by another computer-generated animation showing a bipedal grey and black robot walking on the same checkered floor, with a UI panel on the left displaying "atlas" as the "Actor" and a list of body parts like "pelvis", "ltorso", etc. The video then returns to the black screen with the code and text definitions.

The video opens with a computer screen displaying a 3D simulation environment of a bipedal robot, "Atlas," standing on a checkered ground. A menu on the left shows "atlas" selected, with options for "Actor," "Custom actor color," "Reset Actor Materials," "Bodies," "DOFs," and "Pose Override," followed by a detailed list of robot body parts like "pelvis," "ltorso," and "head." At 0:01, the scene transitions to a man with short, light brown hair and visible arm tattoos, wearing a white t-shirt that reads "ALL YOU NEED IS y = 1/x (with a graph of a hyperbola) x² + y² = 9 (with a graph of a circle) L (a heart shape)," implying "All you need is math and love." He is speaking directly to the camera, using expressive hand gestures. From 0:04, a small, overlaid window in the top-left corner sporadically shows the robot simulation, first falling dramatically, then standing in a more balanced, almost artistic pose, and finally walking, illustrating concepts of "unwanted behavior" and desired states. At 0:13, the screen shifts to a full-frame display of Python-like code, defining several reward/penalty functions (e.g., `base height penalty`, `torque penalty`, `joint acc penalty`, `collision penalty`, `stumbling penalty`, `action rate penalty`), which appear to be components of a reinforcement learning system to guide robot behavior. The scene returns to the man at 0:21, who continues speaking and gesturing with his hands, at one point spreading them wide. As he says the word "terminated" at 0:24, a cartoonish, light blue robot-like skull mask is briefly superimposed over his face, featuring dark eyes, a grin, and visible mechanical details, before disappearing moments later. The background throughout the man's segments is a dark digital rain effect with falling green and white hexadecimal characters.

The video begins with a close-up shot of hands, wearing a blue long-sleeved shirt, typing on a silver laptop keyboard. The laptop screen displays what appears to be a spreadsheet or data table with green and white cells. At the 0:09 mark, the scene transitions to a medium shot of a young man with light brown hair and visible tattoos on his arms, wearing a white t-shirt with mathematical equations ("y = 1/x" and "x² + y² = 9") and the text "ALL YOU NEED IS" printed on it. He is speaking directly to the camera, gesturing with his hands. From 0:15 to 0:20, a black and white cartoon image is overlaid on the left side of the screen, depicting stick figures discussing a "machine learning system" involving a "big pile of linear algebra" and "stirring the pile until they start looking right." The man continues speaking in front of a dark, digital background that resembles falling code or binary data. At 0:26, the scene cuts to an outdoor shot of a black and green bipedal robot, designed to look somewhat humanoid, standing on a sandy or dirt surface. The robot attempts to walk but quickly loses its balance, leaning to its left before collapsing onto the ground in a cloud of dust. In the background, a white fence with "FAIRPLEX" written on it is visible, along with red plastic barriers to the left and a table with equipment to the right. A timestamp "G 16:38 05/06/2015" is displayed in the bottom left corner of this segment.

The video montage shows various humanoid and semi-humanoid robots repeatedly falling in different outdoor environments, illustrating challenges in robot locomotion. The first robot, red and track-footed, falls backward while attempting to open a door against a brick wall, with a timestamp of "01:17:50 06/06/2015" displayed. This is followed by a black and white bipedal robot, bearing a "HIGH VOLTAGE OVERHEAD" sign in the background and a "9:08:53 05/06/2015 UTC" timestamp, falling forward over a pile of concrete blocks. Another black and white robot with blue accents, marked with "6:30:39 05/06/2015 UTC", stumbles and falls sideways on sandy ground near red barriers. A larger, darker bipedal robot marked with "9:14:01 05/06/2015" trips and falls forward onto paved ground after exiting a doorway, again against a brick wall. Lastly, a slender white and red humanoid robot, with "16:46:23 05/06/2015" visible, walks on dirt with a "FAIRPLEX" sign in the background before falling backward. The scene then transitions to a man with short light brown hair, wearing a white t-shirt that says "ALL YOU NEED IS" followed by mathematical equations and their corresponding graphs ("y=1/x", "x²+y²=9"). He has tattoos on his arms and is speaking directly to the camera, gesturing with his hands, against a dark background with green falling digital code.

The video segment opens with a white background displaying the title "AMP: Adversarial Motion Priors for Stylized Physics-Based Character Control" with university logos at the bottom (Berkeley and Shanghai Jiao Tong University). A 3D animated character, resembling a humanoid robot, performs a parkour-like jump over a gap between two elevated platforms, successfully landing on its hands. The scene then transitions to a young man with short brown hair, wearing a white t-shirt that reads "ALL YOU NEED IS y = 1/x, x^2 + y^2 = 9" (representing mathematical functions, implying humor), and tattoos on his arms, speaking directly to the camera against a dark background with flowing green and white binary code. He gestures with his hands, bringing them together. The video then cuts back to a simulation, labeled "Humanoid: Stepping Stones (Cartwheel)" with "Example Clips" on the right, showing the same humanoid character performing a cartwheel across a series of uneven platforms, while other clips on the right show variations of the cartwheel. Text at the bottom states: "Our approach can also be used to train visuomotor policies to traverse irregular environments in different styles." The scene returns to the man, gesturing with his hands. A formula, "Reward Function r_t = r_t^G + r_t^S", appears on a white background, with text below explaining, "Our policies are trained using reinforcement learning with a reward function that". This is elaborated with "r_t^G" labeled as "Task" (showing a dotted path from a blue circle to a red X) and "r_t^S" labeled as "Style" (showing the humanoid character walking), alongside text explaining that it "combines the style objective from the motion prior with a task objective, which specifies high-level goals that the character should fulfill." The man reappears, gesturing, and a white box lists "Target location," "Target heading," and "Target velocity." He continues to gesture, bringing his hands together, as text overlays on the screen: "Reward function that consist of two components specifying: 1) what task a character should perform, and 2) how the character should go about performing that task."

A man with short brown hair, wearing a white t-shirt with a graphic that says "ALL YOU NEED IS" followed by mathematical equations and a coordinate plane, is speaking directly to the camera. He has tattoos visible on his arms. His hands are clasped together in front of him, and he occasionally gestures to emphasize his points. The background is dark, resembling falling binary code with white numbers and letters. On the left side of the screen, white text is overlaid, reading: "Reward function that consist of two components specifying: 1) what task a character should perform, and 2) how the character should go about performing that task." This text likely explains the criteria for a reward function in the context of the man's discussion.

The video opens with a split screen displaying two artistic portraits of women, one labeled "StyleGAN2" and the other "Alias-Free GAN (Ours)," followed by two similar split-screen images of cats. This transitions to a young man with light brown hair, wearing a white T-shirt that reads "ALL YOU NEED IS Y = 1/X X^2 + Y^2 = 9" (All you need is y equals one over x, x squared plus y squared equals nine) with mathematical graphs printed on it, and tattoos on his arms, speaking and gesturing against a dark background of falling digital code. An animated sequence of bright, colorful electric light bursts against a dark, starry background follows. The video then returns to the same man, who continues to speak while text overlays appear: "Motion capture does not have the actions, only observations" and then "=> AMP Only uses the observations as input to discriminator!" This explains that Adversarial Motion Priors (AMP) utilize only observations as input to the discriminator. The scene then shifts to a different man with dark hair, wearing a blue suit and striped tie, smiling as a glowing vintage lightbulb appears above his head, signifying an idea, set against a light blue background. The first man reappears, speaking in the digital code setting, followed by a 3D animation of a glittering, translucent cheetah-like creature with red eyes walking in place. The first man returns once more, speaking with hand gestures, before the video cuts to a screen recording of a GitHub page displaying documentation for "AMP: Adversarial Motion Priors HumanoidAMP.py" within the "IsaacGymEnvs" repository, which includes examples of human motion simulations like spin kicks and walks. The video concludes with the first man speaking and gesturing, emphasizing his points with a finger.

The video segment opens with a young man, wearing a white t-shirt featuring mathematical equations that read "ALL YOU NEED IS y=1/x x^2+y^2=9" (English: "ALL YOU NEED IS y=1/x x^2+y^2=9," representing a hyperbola and a circle), speaking and gesturing with three fingers raised on his right hand against a dark, digital background with scrolling hexadecimal code. This scene transitions into a fragmented display showing four concurrent video clips of a red and black wheeled robot performing various actions, with the text "ETH Zürich" (English: "ETH Zurich") overlaid, indicating the research institution. The clips show the robot balancing on two wheels both indoors and outdoors, and moving on four wheels down a hallway. This then shifts to a single continuous shot of the robot in an indoor lab setting with a white wall and black floor, featuring an "RSL" logo, where it initially balances on two wheels before lowering to all four and moving. The video then cuts to an aerial view of a simulation showing hundreds of these red and black robots scattered across a plain light-colored surface. A circular timer in the top right corner displays increasing time intervals, starting from "02 min" (English: "02 min") and progressing to "25 min" (English: "25 min"). As the timer advances, the robots, initially moving randomly and often falling, gradually demonstrate more controlled and coordinated movements, such as standing upright on two wheels and moving in a more directed fashion, illustrating the on-screen text "Thousand of robots learn in minutes" (English: "Thousands of robots learn in minutes").

The video opens with a split screen showing different demonstrations of a red and silver four-legged robot with wheels: in the top-left, it climbs steps; in the top-right, a person wearing a face mask holds red straps connected to the robot, which stands; and in the bottom-left, the robot walks under a table, with the text "Multiple motion priors" overlaid. From 00:02, a man with light brown hair and tattoos, wearing a white t-shirt that says "ALL YOU NEED IS y=1/x x^2+y^2=9 L O V E" (meaning "All you need is Love" with mathematical equations forming the letters), speaks against a black background with falling green code. Initially, a white humanoid robot is to his left, which then has its head replaced by a smiling older man's head at 00:13. The man gestures with his hands as he talks. At 00:19, the screen transitions to a 3D modeling software (likely Blender), showing several humanoid robot models in various poses. Then, at 00:29, a computer screen displays "Visual Studio Code" and "Isaac Gym," featuring a grid populated by numerous grey humanoid robots running in unison, with interface elements like "Actors," "Sim," "Viewer," and a list of body parts. The screen later shows Python code related to "isaacgymenv.py" and "atlas_amp_base.py," displaying configuration parameters. At 00:47, a meme appears on the left, illustrating "PROGRAMMING AS A STUDENT" (a stick figure stepping on one rake) and "PROGRAMMING AS A SOFTWARE ENGINEER" (multiple stick figures stepping on many rakes). The man continues to speak and gesture, and at 01:02, the screen briefly flashes to black with a single white dot before returning to the man speaking against the code background, using emphatic hand gestures, including pointing his index finger upwards.
